commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for marking tasks as done
Add support for todos, deadlines, and events
Add support for saving and loading tasks
Add support for dates and times parsing
Refactor into Ui, Storage, Parser, and TaskList classes
Add JUnit tests for Parser and TaskList
Configure Shadow pluggin to build executable JAR
Add Javadoc comments to classes and methods
Add support for finding tasks by keyword
Add JavaFX GUI with Waddles theme
Use varargs to join task storage fields
Add JavaFX dependencies for cross-platform JAR
commitResults.messageBody:
The shadow JAR only bundled our own compiled classes, because
JavaFX wasn't declared as a Gradle dependency -- it was only
available locally via the Azul Zulu+FX JDK distribution.
A JAR built this way fails immediately on any computer using a
standard (non-FX) JDK, since JavaFX classes are missing entirely
from the bundled output.
Let's add explicit org.openjfx dependencies, with win/mac/linux
classifiers, so shadowJar has real artifacts to bundle into the
fat JAR.
Declaring all three platform classifiers keeps the JAR portable
across operating systems, rather than only working correctly on
whichever OS happened to build it.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Java assertions to document internal invariants
commitResults.messageBody:
Add `assert` statements (not JUnit assertions) at points where the code
relies on assumptions that should always hold if the rest of the program
is correct, as opposed to user-input errors (which are already reported
via WaddlesException, not assertions):

- Task/Deadline/Event constructors assert their String fields are non-null
  (and non-empty for dates), documenting that callers are responsible for
  validating user input before construction.
- TaskList's constructor and add() assert their arguments are non-null.
- TaskList.find() asserts the keyword is non-null, since Parser#parseFind
  guarantees this.
- Parser#parseTaskIndex asserts its own postcondition (the returned index
  is in bounds), since the preceding range check already handles the
  out-of-range case by throwing.
- Storage#taskToFileFormat asserts it is never asked to serialize null.
- Waddles#getResponse asserts the parsed command word is non-null.

Deliberately NOT added: bounds assertions in TaskList.get()/delete().
TaskList's own tests call delete() with an out-of-range index and expect
IndexOutOfBoundsException to propagate, so out-of-range indices there are
a supported (tested) part of TaskList's public contract, not a
programming error to assert against.

Also enable assertions for `gradlew run` (they were already on by default
for `gradlew test`), so they take effect during normal development use,
not just in tests.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use try-with-resources for file I/O in Storage
commitResults.messageBody:
save() closed its FileWriter with an explicit writer.close() after the
write loop, so an IOException thrown while writing would skip the close
and leak the file handle. load()'s Scanner had the same pattern. Switch
both to try-with-resources so the resource is always closed, even when
an exception propagates out of the loop.

Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Mix1FpDCt2rW5KQ6zGHaSd

commitResults.messageTitle: Narrow overly broad catch(Exception) in Storage.parseLine
commitResults.messageBody:
Catching the generic Exception type silently swallows any bug in this
method, not just the corrupted-data-file case it's meant to handle. The
only realistic failure mode for a malformed line is too few " | "-delimited
fields, which surfaces as ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException; catch that
specific type instead so an unrelated bug (e.g. a NullPointerException
from a future change) fails loudly instead of being treated as "corrupted
data" and silently skipped.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace magic-number substring lengths in Parser with named constants
commitResults.messageBody:
Each parse method hardcoded the length of its own command word (4, 8, 5,
4) as a bare integer to strip the command prefix off the input. These
magic numbers are easy to get wrong if a command word ever changes, and
give the reader no clue what they mean without cross-referencing the
command word used elsewhere. Name each one after the command word it
measures instead.

commitResults.messageTitle: Mark fields that are never reassigned as final
commitResults.messageBody:
Task.description, Storage.filePath, Ui.scanner, TaskList.tasks, and the
date/text fields of Deadline and Event are all set once in the
constructor and never modified afterwards. Declaring them final makes
that immutability explicit and lets the compiler catch any future
accidental reassignment.

commitResults.messageTitle: Extract duplicated add-task logic in Waddles.getResponse
commitResults.messageBody:
The todo, deadline, and event branches each repeated the same four
lines (add to list, format confirmation, save, return) and differed only
in which Parser method produced the Task. Extract addTaskAndRespond(Task)
so that logic exists in one place, per the DRY principle.

commitResults.messageTitle: Convert command dispatch in getResponse to a switch statement
commitResults.messageBody:
A chain of nine if-else-if branches, all testing equality on the same
String, is exactly the case a switch statement is meant for: it states
up front that these are mutually exclusive cases of one value, and
removes the risk of an unbalanced if/else-if/else chain as commands are
added or removed. Behaviour is unchanged; the default case throws the
same "unknown command" WaddlesException as before.

commitResults.messageTitle: Stop silently swallowing FXML load failures
commitResults.messageBody:
DialogBox and Main both caught IOException from FXMLLoader#load() with
just e.printStackTrace(), then kept going: DialogBox would continue with
an uninitialized dialog/avatar Label (a guaranteed NullPointerException
one line later), and Main would exit with no window and no visible
error. Since the FXML files are bundled resources rather than user
input, a failure to load them is a packaging bug that the app cannot
recover from; rethrow as an unchecked IllegalStateException so it fails
fast with a clear cause instead of limping on or exiting silently.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Streams to filter matching tasks in TaskList.find()
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the manual loop that builds up a matches list with a
stream filter/collect pipeline, which reads as a direct statement of
what find() does (select tasks whose description contains the keyword)
rather than how to build that result imperatively.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Streams to build file content in Storage.save()
commitResults.messageBody:
Replace the loop that wrote one line at a time with a stream that maps
each task to its file-format line and joins them with the platform line
separator, so the file's contents are built as a single value before
being written, rather than incrementally via side effects on the
FileWriter. An empty task list is special-cased to still produce a
genuinely empty file, matching prior behaviour.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use Streams to number task lists in Ui
commitResults.messageBody:
formatTaskList() and formatFoundTasks() both hand-rolled the same
"1.<task>\n2.<task>..." numbering with a StringBuilder loop. Extract a
shared formatNumbered(List<Task>) built on IntStream.range/mapToObj/
Collectors.joining, so the two callers share one implementation instead
of two near-identical loops, and the "number each element, join with
newlines" intent is stated directly rather than built up imperatively.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add support for recurring tasks (extension: B-RecurringTasks)
commitResults.messageBody:
Deadlines and events can now repeat on a schedule, e.g. a weekly project
meeting:

  deadline pay rent /by 2024-01-01 /every month
  event standup /from 2024-01-06 /to 2024-01-06 /every day

Design:
- New Recurrence enum (NONE/DAILY/WEEKLY/MONTHLY) knows how to advance a
  LocalDate to its next occurrence and how to parse/serialize itself.
- Task gains isRecurring()/recur() hooks (default: not recurring);
  Deadline and Event override them once a recurrence is set.
- Recurrence requires a structured yyyy-mm-dd date, since advancing a
  free-text date like "Sunday" isn't well-defined; Parser rejects
  "/every" on a task whose date didn't parse, with a message explaining
  why.
- Marking a recurring task done (via "mark") now calls recur() instead of
  leaving it permanently done: this advances its date(s) to the next
  occurrence and resets it to not-done, so the user is naturally
  reminded of the next occurrence rather than the task just vanishing
  from their attention once "done".
- Storage persists the recurrence as an extra trailing field; loading a
  line without that field (from a data file saved before this feature
  existed) defaults it to NONE, so existing save files keep working.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Mix1FpDCt2rW5KQ6zGHaSd

commitResults.messageTitle: Add a "schedule" command to view tasks by date (extension: B-ViewSchedules)
commitResults.messageBody:
schedule 2024-12-01
  schedule today

Shows every deadline due on that date and every event spanning it,
numbered like the existing "list" command, or a friendly message if
nothing's scheduled.

Design:
- Task gains occursOn(LocalDate), defaulting to false (a ToDo has no date
  and can never match). Deadline overrides it to match its own date;
  Event overrides it to match any date within its inclusive from/to span.
  Both only match when their date(s) parsed successfully as yyyy-mm-dd -
  a free-text date like "Sunday" simply won't show up in a schedule view,
  since there's no date to compare against.
- TaskList.findOnDate(LocalDate) filters by occursOn(), mirroring the
  existing find(String) method.
- Parser.parseSchedule accepts either a yyyy-mm-dd date or the word
  "today" for convenience, and rejects anything else with a message
  showing both accepted forms.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add an "undo" command for the most recent change (extension: C-Undo)
commitResults.messageBody:
todo read book
  mark 1
  undo        -> reverts the mark, back to not-done

Minimal (single-level) undo: only the one most recent mutating command
(todo/deadline/event/mark/unmark/delete) can be undone; undoing twice in
a row reports there's nothing left to undo.

Design:
- Task gains copy(), overridden by ToDo/Deadline/Event to include their
  extra fields. A snapshot needs real copies, not just references, since
  Task objects are mutable (markAsDone()) and a later mutation would
  otherwise retroactively change what "undo" restores.
- Waddles.saveUndoSnapshot() deep-copies the task list into a single
  undoSnapshot field right before each mutating command executes; "undo"
  restores it via the new TaskList.setAll() and clears the snapshot.
- TaskList.setAll() mutates the list in place (clear + addAll) rather
  than Waddles reassigning its `tasks` field to a new TaskList, so the
  field can still eventually be made final without conflicting with undo.
